title: Dynamic heuristic acceleration of linearly approximated SARSA(lambda): using ant colony optimization to learn heuristics dynamically
evidence: Table 7: SARSA ABS 103.2, AIBS 96.8; dynamic RS 102.2, 89; static RS 101.4, 75. These are best training trajectory and its index, not final greedy-policy reward. Public static prior artifacts are absent; our priors are regenerated.

title: True Online TD(lambda)
authors: Harm van Seijen and Richard S. Sutton
evidence: Algorithm 2 explicitly initializes eligibility traces at each episode and decays the previous trace before adding the new Dutch contribution. Section 5 extends state features to state-action features. This motivates the numerical control, not a new shaping contribution.

title: Dynamic Potential-Based Reward Shaping
evidence: Maze: 100 repetitions of 1000 episodes, optimal route 41 steps; random changing potentials still converge, but learning is slower in that example. Dynamic shaping need not fail theoretically; a useful potential is required for acceleration. Their multi-agent experiment has a different performance conclusion, so do not generalize the single-agent example.

title: Reward Shaping in Episodic Reinforcement Learning
evidence: Finite trajectories require appropriate terminal potential treatment. Fig 1 counterexample: goal rewards 0 and 100, terminal potentials 1000 and 10 can invert the preference. Our exact arithmetic check sets gamma=.99, producing 990 versus 109.9, and zero terminal potentials restore 0 versus 100.

title: Potential-Based Shaping and Q-Value Initialization are Equivalent
evidence: The publication is JAIR 2003; the arXiv upload is 2011. Under the theorem's assumptions, shaping and suitable Q initialization give equivalent updates and behavior. Our tabular toy verifies 5000 transitions; this identity is not claimed for our action-specific function approximation or changing potentials.

title: Principled Methods for Advising Reinforcement Learning Agents
authors: Eric Wiewiora, Garrison W. Cottrell and Charles Elkan
evidence: State-action potentials require care in interpreting action values and action selection. A fixed state-only potential subtracts the same amount from every action at a state. The 2019 action-dependent raw potential cannot simply inherit the classic state-only policy-invariance argument.

title: Improving the Effectiveness of Potential-Based Reward Shaping in Reinforcement Learning
evidence: DQN MountainCar, gamma=.99, cap 200, 250000 training steps, ten runs, five eval episodes each checkpoint; normalized absolute velocity is transformed exponentially with base 32. Their reward-bias b gives potential shift b/(gamma-1), NOT an additive +b. They report b=1 best and b=0 next; other tested biases and unshaped DQN do not converge in that budget. Our linear |v|/.07 and |v|/.07+1 are only related heuristic controls under gamma=1, cap 1000, SARSA; our +1 is NOT their b=1. No direct numerical ranking across these protocols is warranted.
